programs.title: InfoGurus at the Library: Worker Voice in an Agent-Managed World
outcomes: Explain how an agent-managed, human-governed DAO assigns tasks and drafts proposals while people keep final votes
Practice drafting a workplace proposal suitable for a Proposal Forum debate
Identify which decisions are reserved for humans and why that matters for worker representation

sessions.activity: Read the charter wall: map the mission and the human-reserved actions onto a union decision-making flowchart, comparing with shop-floor voting practice.
Role-play task routing: small groups act as Task Router, Collaborator Scout and workers to negotiate fair task allocation between decision cycles.
Draft a one-page proposal on AI and job security; agents format it, but the room debates and votes as stewards would.
Build a simple outcomes dashboard for a campaign, then critique it against the charter's measurable-outcomes logic.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized proposal drafts and voting-pattern tallies (no names, no employer identifiers) contributed to a shared template library for future DAO proposal training.
programs.consent: Adult learners sign an opt-in consent form at enrollment; anonymization removes names and workplace identifiers; anyone may withdraw their contributions at any time.

programs.title: Young Gurus by the Bay: Library Science and Fair AI Rules
outcomes: Describe how Bibliotheca Alexandrina curates knowledge and how a DAO can govern shared information
Distinguish tasks agents can do from decisions only people should make
Collaborate on a classroom 'charter' with measurable outcomes

sessions.activity: Mini treasure hunt in the library spirit: teams summarize two short sources and present evidence like the Evidence Monitor agent.
Write a class charter: each team proposes one rule and one measurable outcome; the class debates and votes, mirroring human-only final votes.
Craft a proposal for a school improvement idea; peer agents (students) draft, peers debate, teacher acts as steward for the final vote.
Create a poster tracker showing progress on the class charter outcomes and present it gallery-style.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized class charter wording and outcome-tracking poster photos (no student names, faces, or school identifiers) added to a shared civic-education example bank.
programs.consent: Written guardian/parent consent is required before participation and before any poster is photographed; only anonymized group work is shared, and families may withdraw consent at any time.

programs.title: Evidence to Proposal: NGO Practice in an Agent-Managed DAO
outcomes: Apply evidence-monitoring and synthesis workflows to a live NGO issue
Convert synthesized evidence into a structured, human-decided proposal
Track program outcomes against measurable charter targets

sessions.activity: Workshop: run an evidence scan on a chosen issue, practice bias checks and source triangulation modeled on the Evidence Monitor role.
Map an NGO program onto DAO working groups; assign agent-doable tasks vs. human-reserved decisions using the charter list.
Draft and defend a grant-style proposal for human review, following the Proposal & Grant Drafter's never-enact rule.
Design a measurable-outcomes dashboard for one program and stress-test indicators with peers.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized proposal templates and indicator frameworks (organization names and beneficiaries stripped) contributed to a shared NGO proposal-pattern library.
programs.consent: Staff opt in via signed data-sharing agreement; all contributions pass a de-identification checklist; withdrawal and deletion requests honored on demand.

programs.title: Governance by the Harbor: Nonprofit Boards and Human-Reserved Powers
outcomes: Map nonprofit fiduciary duties onto a DAO's human-reserved actions list
Practice steward-level review of agent-drafted proposals
Set measurable outcomes aligned with a public-good mission

sessions.activity: Board simulation: compare your nonprofit's bylaws with the DAO charter, marking which powers must stay human (final vote, amendments, treasury).
Review three agent-drafted proposals as a board; debate, amend, and hold a recorded final vote that only humans cast.
Receive an Evidence Monitor-style briefing and practice asking critical questions of agent-summarized research.
Draft 3-5 measurable outcomes for your mission and plan quarterly tracking with the Progress Tracker model.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized governance checklists and outcome-metric wording (no organization or donor names) added to a shared nonprofit governance pattern set.
programs.consent: Leadership signs an institutional consent covering shared artifacts only after de-identification; individual contributors may opt out; all shared items are reviewable before release.
